name: Hardware-accelerated Multimodality Volume Fusion
definition: A technique to combine multiple volume datasets (e.g., MR and PET) into a single image representation using graphics hardware to solve depth cueing problems and reduce processing time compared to software-based methods.
summary: Hardware-accelerated Multimodality Volume Fusion combines multiple volume datasets into a single image using graphics hardware to solve depth cueing and reduce processing time, distinguishing itself by compositing operations on texture coordinates before alpha blending to avoid manual slice ordering.
